title: Talking Precision Medicine: How Pathologists Are Navigating AI and Digital Pathology
summary: In a Talking Precision Medicine podcast episode, Shakti Ramkissoon, Ph.D., senior vice president of enterprise oncology and diagnostic medical affairs at Labcorp, discusses how pathologists are navigating growing workloads and adopting digital pathology and AI tools.
body_markdown:
In a *Talking Precision Medicine* podcast episode, Shakti Ramkissoon, Ph.D., senior vice president of enterprise oncology and diagnostic medical affairs at Labcorp, discusses how pathologists are navigating growing workloads and adopting digital pathology and AI tools.


**Key takeaway:** Pathologists see AI and digital pathology as tools to augment, not replace, their expertise, but adoption hinges on reimbursement, cost and integration into existing workflows.


Drawing on findings from Labcorp's[Pulse of the Pathologist](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/articles/pulse-pathologist) report, which surveyed 148 practicing pathologists, Ramkissoon discusses how digital pathology can support collaboration across locations and improve access to expertise through remote case review. He also explores AI's potential to automate time-intensive tasks, helping pathologists focus more of their time on case interpretation and clinical consultation.


**Why it matters:** As pathology workloads grow and diagnostic testing becomes increasingly complex, many pathologists see digital pathology and AI as important tools for improving efficiency, supporting collaboration and helping laboratories meet future demand **.**


**Listen to the full episode on**[Talking Precision Medicine](https://www.genialis.com/2026/11/12/the-doctors-doctor-how-pathologists-are-adapting-to-emerging-diagnostics-and-ai-tpm-podcast-63/) **.**
